extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Department of Education Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, institutional compliance officers, school administrators, and legal counsel/stakeholders commenting on Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations describing substantive standards, procedural requirements, cost/impact assumptions, and implementation guidance for recipients of Federal financial assistance. Covers definitions, grievance procedures, notice/training/recordkeeping obligations, Title IX Coordinator duties, and regulatory impact analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR enforcement: notification before termination or DOJ referral
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR cannot pursue termination of Federal financial assistance or refer a matter to the Department of Justice unless a recipient refuses to voluntarily correct a violation after the Department has notified the recipient of the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provides notice and an opportunity to voluntarily correct prior to termination or DOJ referral. OCR also makes resolution agreements publicly available via its website database and will continue to highlight notable cases as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provision of the final regulations is intended to operate independently; the potential invalidity of one provision should not affect the other provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severability clauses in part 106 (including §§ 106.9, 106.16 (redesignated), 106.24, 106.48 (redesignated), 106.62, 106.72, and 106.82) continue to apply. The Department explains that it would have adopted remaining provisions even if one were found unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures: objective evaluation and prohibition on status-based credibility determinations (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include an objective evaluation of all evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible and prohibit credibility determinations based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific procedural requirement; it is intended to ensure fair, evenhanded procedures and avoid bias against complainants or respondents based solely on their status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sex discrimination (bases that involve consideration of sex) (§106.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation lists bases of discrimination that involve consideration of sex: sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bases are distinct from various forms of sex discrimination (e.g., sex-based harassment, sexual violence, prevention of participation consistent with gender identity) addressed elsewhere in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer and coordinate supportive measures as appropriate for parties experiencing sex discrimination or sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures may include counseling for a party who is experiencing suicidal ideation. The Department increased its model assumption regarding the number of incidents resulting in an offer of supportive measures when estimating burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact modeling: small-entity assessment assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis, the Department used an enrollment-based alternative size standard to classify 'small' institutions of higher education rather than the SBA revenue threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains its methodology (see 87 FR 41564), assumes small IHEs on average conduct the same number of investigations per year as all IHEs (noting this likely overstates costs), and considered subsets of very small institutions using IPEDS/NCES data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate for Title IX Coordinator policy-review time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department increased its estimate of the number of hours necessary for a recipient's Title IX Coordinator to review regulations, revise grievance procedures, and assess related training requirements from 6 hours to 12 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change increased first-year cost estimates; the Department explains this update was made 'out of an abundance of caution' in response to commenter concerns about burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'sex-based harassment' (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final definition expands on prior definitions (including hostile-environment harassment) to cover conduct that constitutes sex discrimination and to effectuate Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered alternatives and concluded the final wording best captures the benefits intended; it estimates inclusion of additional forms of sex discrimination may result in about a 10 percent increase in investigations annually, but commenters provided no data to change the estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination publication requirements (§106.8 and §106.8(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must publish a notice of nondiscrimination, but the final regulations account for space/format limitations and allow a short-form notice option when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The short-form notice is a one-sentence statement that the recipient prohibits sex discrimination in any education program/activity and that individuals may report to the Title IX Coordinator, together with a link to the full notice on the website. Recipients may include notices in print or electronically consistent with how they distribute the materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training frequency and triggers (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Training is required promptly upon hiring or a change of position that alters an employee's duties under Title IX, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training obligations for notification duties are expected to be straightforward and can be incorporated into existing training sessions. The Department considered impacts on small entities and concluded costs will not impose an unreasonable burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements adjusted (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed the proposed requirement that recipients maintain all records documenting actions taken to meet obligations under §§ 106.40 and 106.57 and no longer requires training materials to be publicly available on a recipient's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations require training materials to be made available upon request for inspection by members of the public. The Department retained its burden estimate for recordkeeping to ensure estimates fully capture associated burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Title IX to hostile environments with extraterritorial conduct (§106.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must address a sex-based hostile environment under its education program or activity even when some conduct alleged to contribute to the hostile environment occurred outside the recipient's program/activity or outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.11 does not require recipients to investigate conduct that occurred outside the United States per se; the Department has no basis to develop specific cost estimates for extraterritorial investigations and expects such investigations will be few.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to address sex discrimination and employee notification standard (§106.44 and §106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'actual knowledge' standard for sexual harassment was removed for certain applications; notification requirements were modified to require an employee with notification duties to take action when the employee has information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs associated with notification requirements are considered as part of training expenses; the Department rejects the view that these requirements necessarily impose unconstitutional restrictions on speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator obligation to monitor and ability to delegate (§106.44(b) and (f); §106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators have a duty to monitor for barriers to reporting and to respond to patterns, trends, and risk factors, but may delegate specific duties provided a Title IX Coordinator retains ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department offered examples of low-cost monitoring methods (e.g., incorporating questions into training materials, roundtables/listening sessions) and de minimis steps to remove barriers (e.g., reminding about reporting options, reporting employees who discourage reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness of complaint procedures and expected benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require fair, evenhanded procedures for investigating and resolving complaints of sex discrimination so that complainants receive appropriate support and procedures are fair to all involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department asserts these benefits advance educational equity, strengthen protections for students facing discrimination (including sexual orientation and gender identity), and the modest costs are justified by the benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of Title IX authority (sex offender registration and other matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not have authority under Title IX to require individuals found responsible for sexual assault to register as sex offenders; sex offender registration is governed by other Federal, State, or local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, the final regulations do not alter other Department civil rights regulations (Title VI, Section 504, ADA); those laws continue to be enforced independently and complaints may be filed under them where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive activities not required by the regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the final regulations do not require certain measures (e.g., advertising free legal resources, availability of rape kits and drug tests, allowing student representatives from community organizations in discussions), nothing in the regulations precludes a recipient from taking these actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarifies that recipients retain flexibility to provide additional resources or practices that are not mandated by Title IX.
